environment.description: Deployed on ECS Fargate with an Application Load Balancer. The ALB has a fixed-response action rule that adds response headers via a Lambda@Edge-equivalent mechanism (ALB action type 'fixed-response' is NOT used; instead, the downstream Envoy sidecar proxy in the task definition injects headers). The Envoy sidecar is configured with an HTTP lua filter that appends 'Content-Security-Policy: default-src \'self\'; script-src \'self\' https://cdn.example.com; object-src \'none\'' to ALL responses passing through port 8080. Additionally, the ECS task definition sets the container security context with 'readonlyRootFilesystem: true' and the task role has no permissions to send signals cross-container. The Fargate platform version 1.4.0 isolates the network namespace such that only the Envoy sidecar can reach port 8080, and external traffic arrives via the ALB -> Envoy -> app path. The Envoy filter chain is defined in a ConfigMap mounted at /etc/envoy/envoy.yaml with a typed_config using envoy.filters.http.lua with inline_code that sets the CSP header on every response before forwarding to the downstream client.

config.envoy_lua_filter: function envoy_on_response(response_handle) response_handle:headers():add('Content-Security-Policy', "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://cdn.example.com; object-src 'none'") end
config.network_mode: awsvpc, only envoy sidecar exposed to ALB target group
config.signal_isolation: Fargate PID namespace isolation, no cross-container signal capability
